newsitem.title: MEXICO: Television Azteca threatens to sue rival. [CORRECTED 20:22 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Television Azteca threatens to sue rival. [CORRECTED 20:22 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects headline and first paragraph to read that Television Azteca is threatening to sue Grupo Televisa SA de CV, and not the other way round)
Mexico's two top television barons took an increasingly vicious public spat another round on Monday, with Television Azteca threatening to sue Grupo Televisa SA de CV.
The dispute pits Emilio "El Tigre" Azcarraga, head of Grupo Televisa, the world's biggest Spanish-language television network, against Ricardo Salinas Pliego of upstart competitor Television Azteca.
At the center of it all is the jailed Raul Salinas de Gortari, brother of disgraced former president Carlos Salinas de Gortari.

Salinas Pliego (no relation to the ex-president) and TV Azteca took out a two-page advertisement in the Mexico City daily Reforma on Monday, denouncing "20 lies" allegedly perpetrated by Azcarraga and Ricardo Rocha, a journalist who conducts Televisa's "Behind the News" investigative program.

In two recent Televisa programs, Rocha reported that Raul Salinas was a partner in TV Azteca, a former state-owned network, and denounced allegedly shady practices in the privatization process that awarded the TV Azteca concession to Salinas Pliego.

"Televisa has put out a series of lies about TV Azteca," the advertisement said. "Now they want to close 'totally and definitively' the matter. Nonetheless, this cannot be concluded when they have slandered us."
The ad, which disputed point by point 20 assertions made by Televisa, also said TV Azteca was "obligated" to sue Azcarraga and Rocha for "defamation."
The squabbling began on June 28 when Reforma revealed that Salinas Pliego, also the head of major retailer Grupo Elektra SA de CV, had received a $29 million transfer from Raul Salinas.
After initially denying any link, Salinas Pliego acknowledged receiving money from Raul Salinas but has repeatedly denied that Raul had anything to do with either TV Azteca or Elektra.
TV Azteca retaliated with a series of ads alleging that Televisa's ratings were slumping and telling advertisers they could not trust Televisa's promised audience figures.
